summary: Unexpected retroactive invoice increase after tool-calling tokens not reflected in meter — request explanation and provisional credit
description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightServe reports a retroactive invoice increase of $7,400 for the period 2026-02-12 to 2026-02-18 after our billing system applied a catch-up charge. They assert the usage spike corresponds to ramped production traffic that heavily used our function-calling / tool invocation feature.

Impact:
- Customer saw a finalized invoice line item labeled 'Retroactive API usage adjustment' representing tokens that were not present in near-real-time usage dashboards.
- Invoice adjustment triggered finance hold and internal escalation for their procurement team. Customer is asking for a detailed breakdown of the retroactive tokens and a provisional credit while we investigate.

Environment:
- Dedicated deployment (customer-managed VPC) served from us-east region.
- Primary model: vicuna-13b-redwood-quantized pinned during period.
- App pattern: server streams chat to users, uses function calls that trigger asynchronous external HTTP tool invocations that return snippets aggregated into the final chat completion.

Steps to reproduce (as described by customer):
1) Send chat request that triggers function call to external tool A (HTTP webhook).
2) Tool A returns a 2.5KB JSON payload; customer code attaches it to the prompt and continues the chat session.
3) Repeat at scale (concurrent sessions ~450) over a 6-hour window.

Observed behavior / logs provided:
- Customer shows dashboard slices (hourly) missing ~11M tokens until 2026-02-19 when a backfill job recorded them and billing postback created the invoice adjustment.
- Sample request IDs provided: req-378245, req-378812, req-379001.
- Customer attached support logs showing function-call-wait TTLs and a sequence of 2026-02-15 14:xx:xx entries from edge-proxy: "tool-response-delayed, streamed-payload-attached".

Business ask:
1) Show exact token attribution for the retroactive invoice line (per-hour, per-request if possible).
2) Explain root cause and why tokens were not visible in dashboards in near-real-time.
3) Provide provisional credit while investigation completes; customer requests a hold on collections for the disputed line.
4) Recommend mitigations to avoid recurrence (config suggestions or SDK/usage guidance).

Additional context:
- Customer uses our SDK v1.8.2 with streaming enabled. They also have a dedicated capacity contract which normally pins to reserved capacity, but they briefly exceeded dedicated throughput and fell back to hosted routing on 2026-02-16 (customer-supplied metric).
- Finance/AR contact: melissa@brightserve.ai (copied).

2026-03-01 13:05 - SRE (Maya Liu): Observed elevated postback-latency for dedicated proxy between 2026-02-15T13:30 and 2026-02-16T02:00 UTC. Hypothesis: delays caused batched postbacks to be written after the invoice window closed, triggering retroactive adjustments.
2026-03-02 08:22 - Support (Liam Oconnor): Reached out to customer to request additional request IDs and their streaming session IDs. Asked for permission to share reconciler logs masked for PII.

2026-03-02 14:50 - Customer (Melissa, BrightServe): Sent additional request IDs and confirmed they use tool-invoke pattern; says they saw zero tokens on 2026-02-15 in dashboard but high backend counts in their service logs.

2026-03-03 10:12 - Metering Eng (Ravi Patel): Found pattern in reconciler logs where 'tool-attach' events were treated as non-consumptive until external payload arrived, then dedup/merge logic did not emit timely per-request postbacks if payload arrived after the hourly bucket flush. Added pointer to internal issue INT-2248.

2026-03-03 15:30 - Support (Liam Oconnor): Provisionally added a 50% credit on the disputed line while engineering investigates; finance notified. Customer acknowledged and requested timeline for final resolution.

2026-03-04 09:05 - SRE (Maya Liu): Mitigation deployed to change reconciler retry window from 30s to 5m for tool-attach events; monitoring in place to ensure late postbacks are captured before bucket finalization.

2026-03-04 12:00 - Support (Liam Oconnor): Updated customer with mitigation and provisional credit details. Promised a full token-level CSV export within 3 business days and a postmortem summarizing cause and fix.
investigation_notes: Reconciler timeline: postback-reconciler-02 processed a backlog on 2026-02-19 that included events timestamped 2026-02-15 to 2026-02-16.

Root hypothesis: 'deferred-attach' flow for function/tool results delayed emission of token-count postbacks. When external tool payloads arrived after bucket closure, reconciler applied them as retroactive adjustments rather than realtime metrics.
Edge proxy had intermittent latency caused by a circuit breaker oscillation; during oscillation many streaming sessions completed after finalization of hourly buckets.
Dedup logic: requests that previously sent a 'placeholder' postback were not correctly updated when final tokens were appended, causing temporary zero lines on dashboards.
Reproducer notes: Simulated function-calling where tool response delay > 90s, observed identical missing-hour dashboard entries locally with reconciler in current config.
resolution_notes: Temporary measures: Applied provisional 50% credit to disputed invoice line on 2026-03-03 (credit memo CM-2026-031). Collections hold applied to that line pending final reconciliation.

Engineering mitigation: Increased reconciler postback retry window for tool-attach events and patched dedup/merge logic to emit immediate 'finalized' postback when external payload attaches within retry window. Deployed 2026-03-04.

Long-term follow-up: Scheduled metric-level test coverage for deferred-attach flows, and a config flag for customers to opt into synchronous token accounting if they need strict near-real-time dashboards.
Customer deliverables: Will provide token-level per-hour CSV export and reconciliation report by 2026-03-07. Final credit / invoice adjustment to be applied after report and customer confirmation.
Postmortem link (to be created): will be appended once written.
public_resolution_summary: Retroactive invoice line caused by late-arriving token postbacks from function/tool attach flow. We provisionally credited 50% while engineering deployed reconciler timing fixes and dedup patches. Full token-level reconciliation and final credit will follow.
next_steps: Complete token-level CSV export and send to customer by 2026-03-07.
Finalize postmortem and attach to ticket; include timeline and CI tests.
Confirm final credit amount with finance after reconciliation and close dispute per customer agreement.
Monitor reconciler metrics for 72 hours post-deploy to ensure no further late postback retrocharges.
